info.title: OddsRelay API
info.description:
The OddsRelay odds API: matched boards, the raw board, discovery, coverage and status, as served at `https://api.oddsrelay.io`. Every route is `GET`; a trailing slash is ignored; an unknown path is 404 `not_found`; any other method is 405 `method_not_allowed` (a `HEAD`'s 405 has no body). A request that carries a body (none is read) is answered with `Connection: close`, and its connection ends.

## Keys
Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`, never in the query string. Server keys start `or_live_`; browser and dashboard keys start `or_pub_`, answer only calls from their own website's `Origin` (else 403 `origin_not_allowed`), and get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoing that exact origin (never `*`). A browser's CORS preflight (`OPTIONS` with an `Origin`) is answered 204. Keyless routes: `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/spotlight`, `/v2/coverage` without a key header, `/v2/openapi.json`.

## Order of checks
The per-address shield (429 `too_many_from_address`), the key (401), the account's flood cap (429 `too_many_requests`), a suspended account (403 `account_suspended`; `/v2/usage` still answers), a browser key's website (403), then the route's own checks, each described on its operation. Every refusal is free.

## Tokens
One token pool per account, reset monthly; a trial's pool is one-off, so its reset is the trial's end when that comes first. A call's price comes from the request (the product and its filters), never from the reply's size, with one exception: a historical odds file costs `regions.<code>.historical.file_per_mb` for every started 1,000,000 bytes of its size. `/v2/pricing` publishes the table, `quote=true` prices any data request for free, and discovery, `/v2/usage`, `/v2/pricing`, 304s, replies with no events and every refusal are free. A price above the balance is 402 `insufficient_tokens`. Every reply to a valid key carries `X-Tokens-Cost`, plus `X-Tokens-Used`, `-Remaining`, `-Limit` and `-Reset` whenever the balance is known (`unlimited` on an unlimited account).

## Flood cap
One cap per account, per 10 seconds and per minute (dashboard keys have their own), plus a cap on requests in flight; `GET /v2/usage` `flood_cap` gives your account's numbers. Every reply to a valid key after authentication carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining` and `-Reset` for the window with fewer left; over it is 429 `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`. Poll as often as your cap allows: the per-address caps sit well above an account's, so they refuse floods, never a client inside its own cap. The per-address shield answers 429 `too_many_from_address`; the front door's own per-address cap answers 429 with `Retry-After` and an EMPTY body with no `code`, as does its 502.

## Errors
Every JSON error is `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`, plus `type` on a scope 403, `valid` on the four unknown-value 400s and on the four `*_not_in_plan` 403s (`bookmaker_not_in_plan`, `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `exchange_not_in_plan`: outside your plan's bookmakers or your account's scope; `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope), `products` on an `unknown_market` that another product carries (the products that carry it), the balance fields on 402 and `reason`/`dashboard_url` on `account_suspended`. Branch on `code`. `request_id` equals the reply's `X-OddsRelay-Request-Id` (a 405 carries it in the body only).

## Account scope
An account can carry a scope: per product, the sports, markets, bookmakers and exchanges it may read (raw's one `bookmakers` list names venues of both kinds). A product outside it is 403 `not_in_key_scope` for every key on the account; a value a call names outside it is 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan` or `exchange_not_in_plan` with `valid` (the scope's list for that product), `quote=true` included; a filter the call leaves out is trimmed to the scope, before the price. `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope (`scope`, `scope_version`; both null when the account has none). A scope that cannot be applied answers every data route and keyed `/v2/coverage` 503 `temporarily_unavailable`, never the unscoped data.

## Strict inputs
Each route reads the parameters listed on it; any other parameter, or one sent twice, is 400 `bad_request` naming it. `region` is one lowercase code; missing means `uk`.

## Gzip
Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses): bodies over 1 kB are then gzip. A request that refuses gzip (`Accept-Encoding` naming `gzip` or `x-gzip` with `q=0`, `*;q=0` with no gzip above 0, or `identity` alone: Python's `urllib` and `http.client` send `identity` unless told otherwise) gets plain bodies, but `standard`, `dutching` and raw answer it 400. A request with no `Accept-Encoding` gets plain bodies: the front door decompresses them and keeps the gzip representation's `ETag`. `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/spotlight`, `/v2/health`, `/v2/usage`, quotes and errors are always plain.

## Caching
Data replies (never a `quote=true` price), `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events`, `/v2/events/state`, `/v2/events/changes` and `/v2/bookmakers` carry `ETag`, a label of the decompressed content; send it as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged body is 304 with no body, free. Keyed replies are `Cache-Control: private, max-age=2, must-revalidate` and `Vary: Authorization, Accept-Encoding, Origin`.

## Freshness
`meta.processed_at` and `X-Processed-At` are a board's time; `X-OddsRelay-Version` is the publish instant of the board version served (epoch ms), the same on every route for one publish; `meta.last_seen` (matched boards) and `last_seen` (keyed `/v2/coverage`) are when each venue and sport was last read; raw's `last_update` is when a venue's market last changed. The API cuts no row for age, but a venue whose latest read is older than its own window (twice its longest recurring gap between reads, at most 150 seconds, bet365 300) is left off the boards until it is read again.

## Versions
`/v2` is frozen as of 2026-09-21: from that date it takes additions only, meaning a new route, parameter, field, value or code that a client coded against `/v2` can ignore. A breaking change is anything that client cannot ignore: a route, field, value or code removed or renamed, a type or meaning changed, a new required input, or a refusal where there was an answer. A client must accept fields, values and codes it does not know. A breaking change ships only under a new path, `/v3`, announced at least 6 months ahead by email and in the changelog, and `/v2` is kept for at least 12 months after `/v3` ships. Anything scheduled to end carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on its replies. Event ids are opaque, and an event's id never changes for its fixture: once an id has been served, every later answer for that fixture carries it. If two ids turn out to be one fixture, the one served first is kept, and the other is listed in the event's `previous_ids` and still answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds`. Changing a served id is a breaking change. `X-OddsRelay-Api-Version` equals `info.version`, on every reply but `/healthz`, a `HEAD`'s 405 and the empty-bodied 429s and 502; additions never change it, and a new label comes only with a new version path.

get.description:
The six matched boards: each event's bookmaker back prices beside the exchanges' lay prices (`dutching`: back legs that cover every outcome, grouped by `dutch_id`; `each-way` and `extra-place`: each-way terms against win and place lays).

**Checks, in this order** (each refusal is free): the per-address shield, the key, the account's flood cap, a suspended account, a browser key's website, the API version; then `type` (404 `unknown_type`), `region`, the region in the key (403 `region_not_in_scope`), the product in the key (403 `not_in_key_scope`), the product in the region (403 `product_not_in_region`: a region serves the products its `coverage_model` on `/v2/regions` names — every international code `raw` alone, so all six matched types answer this 403 there; a region with no exchange serves only dutching and raw); then the parameters: each one this route reads, once; `format`, `oddsFormat` and `dateFormat` values; on `standard` and `dutching` decimal ISO only and gzip accepted (400 `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`); then the filters (400 unknown values, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`, then your account's scope: 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan`, `exchange_not_in_plan`; and your plan's bookmaker list), then `quote=true`, the price (402), and the board (503 while it is not ready).

**Filters** cut the whole board's events in order: sport and kick-off, then markets, then back offers by bookmaker and lay offers by exchange; an outcome left with no back or no lay goes, then empty markets and events. On `dutching`, naming venues returns each market's best set made only from the named venues, bookmakers and exchanges alike: a set whose every leg is named comes back unchanged, any other is replaced by the best set the named venues make by the same rules (one leg per outcome, each at a different bookmaker or exchange, sites that share one price feed counting as one; rated 100 / Σ(1 / price) inside the board's bounds), or left out when they make none. Naming none returns the best set across every venue. A filtered reply is priced on its filters (`/v2/pricing`); the kick-off window is never priced.

**Freshness**: `meta.processed_at` and `X-Processed-At` are the board time; `meta.last_seen` is each venue and sport's last read. The API drops no row for age; a venue not read within its own window (at most 150 seconds, bet365 300) is off the board until its next read.

**Conditional requests**: send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match`; an unchanged body is a 304 with no body, free. A reply with no events is free.

get.description:
Every venue's prices per event, one page at a time: bookmakers as `{name, price}`, exchanges quoting a lay side as `{name, back_price, lay_price, available}`. Served gzip only: a request refusing gzip is 400 `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`.

**Checks, in this order**: the per-address shield, the key, the flood cap, a suspended account, a browser key's website, the API version; `region`, the region and `raw` in the key; the parameters (each one this route reads, once) and their values; the filters (400 unknown values, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan`, then your account's scope: 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan`); `includeLinks` and `includeLiquidity`; `limit`; `cursor`; gzip; the raw board (503 `raw_not_enabled`); the page (503 while it cannot be cut); `quote=true`; the price (402).

**Paging**: pages are ordered by (kick-off, event id) and a cursor resumes strictly after the last event it saw, so an event that leaves the board between pages never restarts the walk. The accepted limit: an event whose kick-off moves across the cursor during a walk can appear twice or be missed. Dedupe by event `id`, and take a missed event on the next walk. A cursor expires 300 s after it was issued.

**Following changes**: walk with `updatedSince` set 15 s before the start of your previous walk; `last_update` is when a venue's market last moved (see the schema for what it is not), and the first page's `meta.removed` names every event, bookmaker and market that left the board since then (apply it first; `meta.removed_since` later than your `updatedSince` means walk once without it).

**Several regions in one call**: `region` takes a comma list of international codes (`region=us,global`; every code but `uk`, which is asked alone). The reply is ONE board: each event once, with the bookmaker rows of every listed region (each row's `region` says which); an event two regions list under one id is one event, and a fixture they list too differently to join stays two, as on one code. Every filter is read against the listed regions together: a bookmaker of any listed region may be named (one outside them all is 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`), and an account's bookmaker list is its list in each. One cursor pages the merged board; it holds a position only, so keep one `region` value for a whole walk. `updatedSince` and `meta.removed` work as on one code. The price is the listed regions' prices ADDED: each region's own price for the same filters (`bookmakers` counted in the region each belongs to; a region none of the named bookmakers belongs to adds nothing), so a whole walk costs what the regions' walks cost one by one, and `quote=true` says it. One call is one usage row, its region the sorted list (`global,us`). The event-state routes stay one code per call: a `since` token from any international code follows every international code, so one token covers a list.

**Price**: a page pays its share of the query's price (its prices over all the query's events' prices, at least 1; `eventIds` and `requireBookmakers` narrow the page, never the query), so a whole walk pays the query's price (narrowed by `eventIds` or `requireBookmakers`, only its kept events' share of it); a recent `updatedSince` pays a reduced share. `quote=true` prices this page.

get.description: The event-state register's snapshot: each event's FATE in one region's lane, judged across every venue we read, not only your bookmakers — `scheduled` (not known to be over or withdrawn), `started` (pre-match is over), `gone` (withdrawn, confirmed; not issued yet: the changelog dates its start) or `merged` (a duplicate of `merged_into`). Free, like `/v2/events`; it counts against your flood and in-flight caps. Rows are ordered by id and paged with `cursor` (300 s); each page is read in one transaction with the log position in `meta.since`: keep the FIRST page's and follow `/v2/events/changes` from it with the same `region` and filters. List your events from raw (`/v2/odds/raw`), and use these routes for each event's fate: keep an event listed while its state is `scheduled`, even when raw has no prices for it right now; hide it, but keep its row, while it is `started`, `gone` or `merged`. The register covers the ids raw serves in the lane; an id served only on the matched boards answers in `meta.unknown_ids`. Your account's scope is a ceiling: rows outside its sports are never returned. The client recipe and the windows table (K, G and C per sport) are in the docs.

get.description: The event-state register's ordered log for one region's lane, from `since` (a snapshot's FIRST `meta.since`, then each reply's `meta.next_since`). Free, like `/v2/events`. Each change carries the FULL row after it (`event`): replace your row with it whenever its `seq` is above yours, whatever `change` says, including values you do not know. A call scans at most 50,000 positions of the log: while `meta.more` is true call again at once with `meta.next_since` (a reply can be empty and still have `more`), then store `meta.next_since` and call again in about 30 s. Filters run on each change as it was written: send exactly your snapshot's filters. A `descriptors` change passes `sports` and `leagues` when the event passes before or after it (an event that leaves your filters still reaches you with its new row); a `kickoff` passes a kick-off window when its old or new kick-off is inside; a `merged` change passes when the merged id does. A kick-off window selects on each change's kick-off at the time of the change: use a fixed window (re-snapshot to move it) or none. On 410 `since_expired`, snapshot again, then look up with `/v2/events/state?eventIds=` every id you hold that the new snapshot lacks, before you hide it. Your account's scope is a ceiling, judged before or after each change like `sports`.

get.description:
`/v2/odds/raw` as it was served at `date`, bookmakers and exchanges (`bookmakersOnly=true`: bookmakers alone; BETDAQ never): the same envelope and the same event objects, cut to `sports` and paged the same way (by kick-off, then id; at most 250 events a page), plus `historical`, `timestamp` (the board version used: the latest at or before `date`), `previous_timestamp`, `next_timestamp` and `complete`. `sport_key`, `sport_title` and `competition_key` are the ones the live feed served the event: its first league and competition, held for the event's life (an event last served before 2026-11-13 12:45 UTC has none held: its league as recorded and `competition_key` null). The `sports` filter selects on `sport_key` (the key or its start) and the sport name (`football`), not on `competition_key` as the live feed's does: to get one competition, ask its league's key and keep the events whose `competition_key` is the competition's — the English Premier League is `sports=soccer_premier_league` (every league named Premier League: 56 events at 2026-11-16T12:00:00Z, the 21 English ones with `competition_key` `soccer_english_premier_league`), or `sports=soccer` for every league its events were first served under. An event last served before 2026-11-13 12:45 UTC has `competition_key` null. A race names its course (`venue`) as the live feed spells it; one recorded before 2026-11-13 12:49 UTC carries it only where the archive proves it (23,035 of 24,262 races 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-12; the rest carry no `venue`). `previous_ids` are the merges known at that instant. Served gzip only. THE RELEASE LAG: history is released a UTC day at a time, cut the night after the day; the newest instant served is the archive's newest checkpoint's board version plus one hour, and a later one is 400 `date_out_of_range` with `latest`.

**Checks, in this order** (the live feed's own): the per-address shield, the key, the flood cap, a suspended account, a browser key's website, the API version; `region` (uk or one international code; outside the regions your key reads 403 `region_not_in_scope`), `historical` in the key; the parameters (each one this route reads, once) and their values; the instant(s); the venues (400 unknown, 403 outside your plan, 403 `exchange_history_unavailable` for any exchange while exchange history is switched off; `bookmakersOnly=true` beside an exchange filter is 400); your account's scope (403 with `valid`; a sport, market or venue left out is the scope's list); `quote=true`; the price (402).

region.name: region
region.description: ONE lowercase region code (`/v2/regions` lists yours). Missing means `uk`: on a data route only when your key covers `uk`, else 400 `region_required` naming your account's home region or another code your key reads; on discovery and keyless routes always. A comma list is 400 `bad_request` on every route but `/v2/odds/raw` (which reads a list of international codes as one board: see its `region`); the parameter sent twice or an uppercase code is 400 `bad_request` on every route; an unknown code, or one with no live bookmaker here, is 404 `unknown_region`; on a data route, a known code that does not serve the route's product is 403 `product_not_in_region` instead (`standard?region=au`).

rawRegion.name: region
rawRegion.description: ONE lowercase region code, or a COMMA LIST of international codes read as one board (`region=us,global`). Missing means `uk`: only when your key covers `uk`, else 400 `region_required` naming your account's home region or another code your key reads. THE LIST: two or more codes, each once, in any order (`global,us` and `us,global` are the same call: the codes are sorted, and `meta.region` and `meta.regions` say which were read); every code but `uk` — `uk` in a list is 400 `bad_request` ("'uk' is asked in its own call: send ?region=uk alone…"), and so is a code named twice or an empty item. Every listed code is checked as a single code is: uppercase is 400 `bad_request`; an unknown code, or one with no live bookmaker, is 404 `unknown_region` naming it; a code your key does not read is 403 `region_not_in_scope` naming the first such code in sorted order. The parameter sent twice is 400 `bad_request` (`?region=us&region=global` is not a list). The list is `/v2/odds/raw`'s alone: every other route, `/v2/odds/event/{id}` included, takes one code per call.

quote.description: `true` (also `1`, `yes`, `on`): price this exact request instead of serving it. 200 `{cost, remaining, rate_card}`, free, every check before the price still applies; any other value is an ordinary request.

sports.name: sports
sports.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: a sport key or a prefix of one as `/v2/sports` lists them (`horse_racing`, `soccer`), lowercased. A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Unknown is 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid` (the sport key bases). A known value with nothing on the board is an empty 200, free. A value is inside your account's scope when it starts with a scope sport (every `soccer_…` key under `soccer`); outside, 403 `sport_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

bookmakers.name: bookmakers
bookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: bookmaker keys as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them (a listed name is accepted too). A venue that has closed is accepted and ignored: it adds nothing, and a call whose venue lists name only closed venues keeps nothing. Unknown is 400 `unknown_bookmaker` with `valid`; an exchange here is that 400 naming `exchanges` (on `dutching` both lists take venues of either kind, and each market's best set is made from the named venues alone); a venue outside the region is 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`; one outside your plan's bookmaker list or your account's scope is 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan` with `valid` (on `dutching`, an exchange outside the scope is 403 `exchange_not_in_plan`). A plan with a bookmaker list, or an account scope, trims a call naming none to that list.

exchanges.name: exchanges
exchanges.description: Comma-separated, at most 4: exchange keys as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them. A venue that has closed is accepted and ignored: it adds nothing, and a call whose venue lists name only closed venues keeps nothing. Unknown is 400 `unknown_exchange` with `valid`; a bookmaker here is that 400 naming `bookmakers` (on `dutching` both lists take venues of either kind, and each market's best set is made from the named venues alone). Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `exchange_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

markets.name: markets
markets.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: market keys — raw: `h2h`, `over_under`, `handicap`, …; the matched boards: `h2h`, `totals`, …. Each product's keys: keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets` (an international region: `/v2/coverage?region=<code>`, whose `/v2/sports` rows list no market keys); a UK `/v2/sports` row lists the keys seen under its competition. Unknown is 400 `unknown_market` with `valid` (this product's keys) and, when another product carries it, `products`; another product's key may instead be accepted and match nothing. Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `market_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

commenceTimeFrom.description: Events kicking off at or after this ISO-8601 instant (no offset = UTC; a fraction of a second rounds up). Not ISO-8601 is 400; on the matched boards a From after To is 400.

commenceTimeTo.name: commenceTimeTo

rawSports.name: sports

A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Unknown is 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid`. Inside your account's raw scope: a key or prefix starting with a scope sport, a sport name only when it equals one (send `soccer`, not `football`); outside, 403 `sport_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope. A key can hold letters with accents (`soccer_taça_de_portugal`); its spelling without them (`soccer_taca_de_portugal`) is accepted too, so a value never needs percent-encoding.

rawSport.name: sport
rawSport.description: The same as `sports` (what `/v2/events` takes); ignored when `sports` is sent.

leagues.name: leagues
leagues.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: competition names (an event's league or `sport_title`), lowercased. Not checked against a catalogue.

rawBookmakers.name: bookmakers
rawBookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: venue keys of either kind, bookmakers and exchanges, as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them. A venue that has closed is accepted and ignored: it adds nothing, and a call whose venue lists name only closed venues keeps nothing. Unknown is 400 `unknown_bookmaker` with `valid`; outside the region 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`; outside your plan's bookmaker list or your account's raw scope 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan` with `valid`. An account scope's raw list is the whole venue list, exchanges included: left out, trimmed to it (so `exchangesOnly=true` keeps only the exchanges it names).

rawRequireBookmakers.name: requireBookmakers
rawRequireBookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40 venue keys, checked as `bookmakers` is (the same 400 and 403 codes); requiring a venue that has closed keeps nothing. Keeps only the events where EVERY named venue quotes the call's `markets` (with several, at least one of them each), under `exchangesOnly` if set; a venue that lists the event but not the market does not count. `bookmakers` does not narrow this test and `updatedSince` is not part of it: with `updatedSince`, an event carrying every named venue is kept when any venue shown changed, and the page shows only the venues that changed. It narrows events, never venues: every venue the other filters keep is still shown, named or not. `meta.total` and `X-Count` count the events kept. Price: like `eventIds`, it narrows the page and not the query, so a page pays its share of the same call without `requireBookmakers`, and an empty page is free.

rawMarkets.name: markets
rawMarkets.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: market keys raw serves. Raw's keys: keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets.raw`. Unknown is 400 `unknown_market` with `valid` (raw's keys) and, when another product carries it, `products`. Keeps venues quoting one of them, and only those markets. Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `market_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

rawEventIds.name: eventIds
rawEventIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids. An id merged into another (in that event's `previous_ids`) returns that event. Narrows the page, not the query: a page pays its share of the same call without `eventIds`.

updatedSince.name: updatedSince
updatedSince.description: Exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (any other form is 400). Keeps venues whose `last_update` is at or after it, and the events holding one; an event that ARRIVED on the board at or after it (new, back from in-play, or back after an absence), or whose OWN details changed then (kick-off, teams, course, name, competition, `previous_ids`), comes whole, every venue, whatever their `last_update`. Our raw service restarts now and then, and the board then holds still for about a minute: a price that moved meanwhile can be missed by a walk that spans it, so when `meta.processed_at` stood still for 30 s or more between two of your walks, walk the board once without `updatedSince`. The bulk way to follow raw: a recent `updatedSince` pays a reduced share (`/v2/pricing` `recent`). Start the next walk 15 s before the previous one began, and dedupe by event `id`. The first page also carries `meta.removed`: the events, bookmakers and markets that left the board since then (an event `in_play` or `merged` says so), so a delta poller removes them; check `meta.removed_since` — later than your `updatedSince` means walk the board once without it.

includeLinks.name: includeLinks
includeLinks.description: `true`: each venue's `link` (its primary event page; left out when it has none). Default `false`. `true` or `false`, else 400.

includeLiquidity.name: includeLiquidity
includeLiquidity.description: `false`: leave out an exchange's stakes, `available` beside its `lay_price` and `back_available` beside its back price. Default `true`. `true` or `false`, else 400.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The previous page's `meta.next_cursor` (or `X-Next-Cursor`). A cursor is bound to no account and expires 300 s after it was issued: 400 `cursor expired: start again from the first page`; any other shape 400 `cursor not recognised: start again from the first page`.

eventStateCursor.name: cursor
eventStateCursor.description: The previous page's `meta.next_cursor`. This route sends no `X-Next-Cursor` header: page with the envelope. A cursor is bound to no account and expires 300 s after it was issued: 400 `cursor expired: start again from the first page`; any other shape 400 `cursor not recognised: start again from the first page`. With `eventIds` (always one page) it is 400.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Events per page, 1-250 (default and maximum 250). Anything else is 400.

eventsSport.name: sport
eventsSport.description: Required: a sport key or a prefix of one as `/v2/sports` lists them. A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Missing is 400 `missing_param`; unknown 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid`. A key can hold letters with accents (`soccer_taça_de_portugal`); its spelling without them (`soccer_taca_de_portugal`) is accepted too, so a value never needs percent-encoding.

eventsEventIds.name: eventIds
eventsEventIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids. An id merged into another (in that event's `previous_ids`) returns that event.

type.name: type
type.description: A matched board: `standard`, `2up`, `dutching`, `each-way`, `extra-place` or `bog`. The aliases `two-up`, `each_way` and `extra_place` are accepted and served as their canonical slug. Anything else is 404 `unknown_type`.

eventId.name: id
eventId.description: An event id (`or_evt_…`) from raw, a matched board or `/v2/events`. An id that was merged into another (it is in that event's `previous_ids`) answers that event, whose own id is in the body. Not on the raw board now is 404 `unknown_event`.

acceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
acceptEncoding.description: Send `gzip`; with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses the reply. `standard` and `dutching` answer a request that refuses gzip (`identity` alone, as Python's `urllib` sends by default, or `gzip;q=0` or `*;q=0`) with 400 `bad_request`, message `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`; the other four boards answer it plain.

rawAcceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
rawAcceptEncoding.description: Send `gzip`; with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses the reply. The raw board answers a request that refuses gzip (`identity` alone, as Python's `urllib` sends by default, or `gzip;q=0` or `*;q=0`) with 400 `bad_request`, message `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`.

histRegion.name: region
histRegion.description: `uk`, the archive's own region (default), or one international code. Each of the 20 international codes is its own archive of its own venues: bookmakers, and in `ca` also STX (`stx_ca`, Ontario's betting exchange, as /v2/odds/raw serves it there: its back prices under each market's key, its lay prices under `<key>_lay`; `bookmakersOnly=true` leaves it out, and a file's `bookmakers_only` says whether the file holds its rows), recorded from 2026-11-16T05:50Z, the lane's first checkpoint (its first day 2026-11-16: an instant before that day is 400 `date_out_of_range` with `earliest` 2026-11-16T00:00:00.000Z, one inside it before the first checkpoint 404 `no_history`), `gr` from its switch-on at 2026-11-16T18:19Z (a `gr` page asked for before it is empty, and free), with uk's tiers, release lag and rules. Outside the regions your key reads: 403 `region_not_in_scope`; any other code is 404 `unknown_region`.

histDate.name: date
histDate.description: The instant, ISO-8601 to the millisecond (`Z` or an offset; a naive value is UTC). The board served is the board version at or before it. From 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z (the recorded data starts 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z: earlier is 404 `no_history`) to the archive's newest instant — its newest checkpoint's board version plus one hour (checkpoints are cut nightly for the previous UTC day), else 400 `date_out_of_range` (with `earliest` and `latest`). Send a reply's `next_timestamp` or `previous_timestamp` back as `date` to step version by version.

histSports.name: sports
histSports.description: Comma list, up to 20: a sport key or the start of one (`soccer`, `soccer_premier_league`), matched against each event's `sport_key`, never its `competition_key`; on the snapshot route a sport name (`football`) too. Required (The Odds API's historical snapshots are per sport too).

histBookmakers.name: bookmakers
histBookmakers.description: Comma list of bookmaker keys (`/v2/bookmakers`), up to 40; none = every bookmaker. An exchange here is 400 naming `exchanges`.

histExchanges.name: exchanges
histExchanges.description: Comma list of exchange keys (`/v2/bookmakers`), up to 4. While exchange history is switched off, any exchange here is 403 `exchange_history_unavailable`; beside `bookmakersOnly=true` it is 400.

histMarkets.name: markets
histMarkets.description: Comma list of raw's market keys (`h2h`, `over_under`, `handicap`, …; never the matched boards' `totals`), up to 20: a key raw does not carry matches nothing, and venues and markets outside it are left out.

histExchangesOnly.name: exchangesOnly
histExchangesOnly.description: `true`: exchanges alone. While exchange history is switched off, `true` is 403 `exchange_history_unavailable`; beside `bookmakersOnly=true` it is 400.

histEventIds.name: eventIds
histEventIds.description: Comma list of event ids, up to 50; an id merged away by then answers as its survivor.

histLimit.name: limit
histLimit.description: Events per page, 1-250 (default and maximum 250): the page one price buys.

histFrom.name: from
histFrom.description: The window's start, ISO-8601 to the millisecond, from 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z (the recorded data starts 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z) to the archive's newest instant.

histTo.name: to
histTo.description: The window's end (default: `from` + 24 h, or the archive's newest instant if that is earlier). At most 24 hours after `from`, and never after the archive's newest instant (400 `date_out_of_range`, with `latest`).

histRowLimit.name: limit
histRowLimit.description: Rows per page, 1-5000 (default 5000): the page one price buys. A page never splits one board version, so it can hold a few more.

histDay.name: date
histDay.description: A UTC day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, from 2026-10-15 (the recorded data starts 2026-10-17) to the day of the archive's newest instant (a later day is 400 `date_out_of_range`, with `latest`): a day's closing lines are cut the night after it.

histClosingLimit.name: limit
histClosingLimit.description: Events per page, 1-50 (default 50): the page one price buys.

histTier.name: tier
histTier.description: `closing`, `60s`, `5s`, `1s` or `changes`; none = every tier. `closing`, `60s` and `changes` are cut nightly; `5s` and `1s` by arrangement, listed only where a file exists.

histFilesSports.name: sports
histFilesSports.description: Comma list: sport directories a value prefixes (or that prefix it).

histFilesFrom.name: from
histFilesFrom.description: Files of this UTC day or later (an ISO-8601 instant).

histFilesTo.name: to
histFilesTo.description: Files of this UTC day or earlier (an ISO-8601 instant).

histBookmakersOnly.name: bookmakersOnly
histBookmakersOnly.description: `true`: bookmakers alone, no exchange — the answer this route gave before exchanges were added. Default `false` (bookmakers and exchanges; BETDAQ never). `true` or `false`, else 400; `true` beside `exchanges` or `exchangesOnly=true` is 400.

inPlay.name: inPlay
inPlay.description: `exclude` (default): events in play are left out. `include`: in-play and pre-match events, each with `in_play`. `only`: in-play events alone, each with `in_play`. An event is in play when its venues show it in play, not by its `commence_time`, and it keeps its `id` (and its place in the `include` order) when it goes in play; under `include` it is served once. On `/v2/odds/event/{id}`, an event the value leaves out is 404 `unknown_event`; when the event is in play and the value (or its absence) left it out, the message says so on every region: "Event '<id>' is in play: ask with inPlay=include." Costs what the same call without it costs. One of the three, else 400.

matchedInPlay.name: inPlay
matchedInPlay.description: `standard` and `dutching` only: on any other type it is 400 `bad_request` (an unknown parameter). `exclude` (default): events in play are left out, the same reply as the call without it. `only`: in-play events alone, each with `in_play`. An event is in play when its venues show it in play, not by its `commence_time`. Costs what the same call without it costs. One of the two, else 400.

eventRegion.name: region
eventRegion.description: ONE lowercase region code; missing means `uk`. Event ids are shared across regions wherever the two listings can be matched: a fixture `uk` lists carries its `uk` id on any other region, and an id merged across regions keeps answering in `previous_ids` on its own region's routes. Not matched across regions yet, so served under their own region's id: horse and greyhound racing, outright markets, virtual games, and a fixture two regions list too differently to join. `since` tokens still belong to one lane: `uk`, or every other region. A comma list, the parameter sent twice or an uppercase code is 400 `bad_request`; an unknown code, one another service answers, or one whose lane is not switched on here is 404 `unknown_region`.

eventSports.name: sports
eventSports.description: Comma-separated, at most 20, lowercased, judged exactly as raw's `sports`: a row passes when its `sport_key` starts with a value, its sport name (`football`) equals one, its competition is the one a competition key names, or a key one of its venues files it under starts with a value. Unknown is 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid`. Inside your account's scope (the sports of the products your key holds); outside, 403 `sport_not_in_plan`.

eventStates.name: states
eventStates.description: Comma-separated: `scheduled`, `started`, `gone`, `merged`. Default `scheduled`; all four with `eventIds`. Without `eventIds`, any value but `scheduled` needs `commenceTimeFrom` and `commenceTimeTo` at most 7 days apart. Any other value is 400 `bad_request`.

eventStateIds.name: eventIds
eventStateIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids: one page holding each id's own row, plus each merged id's final survivor, deduplicated and ordered by id. `sports`, `leagues` and the kick-off window are not applied, and a survivor is returned whatever its sport, window or state; your account's scope still applies. An id with no row here, or outside your scope, is listed in `meta.unknown_ids`. `cursor` cannot be sent with it.

eventChangeIds.name: eventIds
eventChangeIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids: only their changes. Add a survivor when one of yours is merged.

eventStateLimit.name: limit
eventStateLimit.description: Rows per page, 1-1000 (default 1000). Anything else is 400.

eventChangeLimit.name: limit
eventChangeLimit.description: Changes per call, 1-5000 (default 1000). Anything else is 400.

since.name: since
since.description: Required: the position to follow from, `meta.since` of a snapshot's FIRST page or the previous call's `meta.next_since`. Missing is 400 `missing_param`; not of the form `<epoch>.<seq>` 400 `bad_request`; one this lane can no longer serve 410 `since_expired` with `oldest_since`.

eventDateFormat.name: dateFormat
eventDateFormat.description: `iso` (default, second-precision ISO-8601 UTC) or `unix` (epoch seconds) for `commence_time`, `from_commence_time`, `state_since`, `first_seen`, `at` and `meta.as_of`. `board_version`, `X-OddsRelay-Version` and `meta.processed_at` never change.

X-OddsRelay-Api-Version.description: The API version label, equal to this document's `info.version`. On every reply but `/healthz`, a `HEAD`'s 405 and the empty-bodied 429s and 502.

X-OddsRelay-Request-Id.description: This request's id (`or_req_` + 32 hex), the same value as an error body's `request_id`: quote it when you contact us. On data and discovery 200s, quotes, `/v2/usage` and `/v2/pricing` 200s and every JSON error but a 405; not on 304s, `/v2/health`, `/v2/regions`, `/v2/coverage` 200s or `/v2/odds/event/{id}` 200s.

ETag.description: The content label. Data replies (never a `quote=true` price), `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events`, `/v2/bookmakers` and `/v2/spotlight`: `"c<CRC-32, 8 hex>-<length hex>"` of the DECOMPRESSED body, with `-gz` appended inside the quotes on the gzip representation, so it changes when, and only when, those bytes change. `/v2/pricing` and `/v2/openapi.json`: the body's SHA-256 hex, `-gz` likewise. Send it back as `If-None-Match` for a 304 (weak comparison; `*` matches any).

X-OddsRelay-Version.description: The publish instant of the board version the body was cut from, epoch milliseconds. One publish reads one value on every route that serves it. Present whenever the board version is known.

X-Processed-At.description: The board time, equal to `meta.processed_at` (ISO-8601 UTC, milliseconds). Also on 304s and on `format=bare` replies; never on a `quote=true` price.

X-Count.description: `format=bare` only: the events served (matched boards), or the rows across all pages (raw, `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events`, `/v2/bookmakers`).

X-Next-Cursor.description: `format=bare` only, raw and paged discovery: the next page's cursor, empty on the last page.

X-Tokens-Cost.description: Tokens this reply cost: 0 on a free reply (304, an empty reply, discovery, `/v2/usage`, `/v2/pricing`, a quote and every refusal). On every reply to a valid key, refusals included; never on a 401, on the per-address 429 or on a keyless route.

X-Tokens-Used.description: Tokens the account has used this period. Sent with the other balance headers whenever the balance is known (while the key registry is unreachable a reply can carry `X-Tokens-Cost` alone).

X-Tokens-Remaining.description: Tokens left this period, or `unlimited` on an unlimited account. Sent when the balance is known.

X-Tokens-Limit.description: The account's tokens for the period, or `unlimited`. Sent when the balance is known.

X-Tokens-Reset.description: When the pool resets (ISO-8601 UTC, whole seconds); on a trial, the trial's end when that comes first. Sent when the balance is known.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The account's flood cap for the window with fewer requests left (per 10 seconds or per minute; your numbers are in `/v2/usage` `flood_cap`). On every reply to a valid key after authentication, 429 `too_many_requests` included; never on a 401, the per-address 429 or a keyless route.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying: on every 429 and 503. A 402 never carries it.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: `*` on every GET reply of a keyless route (`/v2/status`, `/v2/spotlight`, keyless `/v2/coverage`, `/v2/openapi.json`), refusals and errors included. A keyed reply never sends `*`: a browser or dashboard key's reply echoes the exact request `Origin` when the key allows it, with `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.

Cache-Control.description: Keyed replies: `private, max-age=2, must-revalidate`. `/v2/status` and `/v2/spotlight`: `public, max-age=10`; keyless `/v2/coverage`: `public, max-age=60`; `/v2/openapi.json`: `public, max-age=300`; `/healthz`: `no-store`.

Vary.description: Keyed replies: `Authorization, Accept-Encoding, Origin`. Keyless `/v2/coverage`: `Authorization, X-Api-Key, Accept-Encoding`. `/v2/openapi.json`: `Accept-Encoding`. JSON errors on `/v2` routes: `Origin`.

Content-Encoding.description: `gzip` when the body is gzip (see the gzip rules in the description).

ErrorBody.description: Every JSON 4xx and 5xx this API writes.

code.description: Stable machine code; branch on this, never on `message`.

type.description: Scope 403s only: which axis refused (`not_in_key_scope` and `product_not_in_region` product; `region_not_in_scope` and `bookmaker_not_in_region` region; `schema_not_in_scope` schema).

valid.description: `unknown_sport` (sport key bases), `unknown_bookmaker`, `unknown_exchange`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan` (your plan's bookmakers, or your account scope's, in the call's region), `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan` and `exchange_not_in_plan` (the scope's list for that product): the values accepted, sorted. `unknown_market`: the market keys this product carries, sorted (keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets`); a key another product carries may also be accepted on this route, and matches nothing here.

products.description: `unknown_market` only, when another product carries the market: those products, sorted, as the `{type}` of `/v2/odds/{type}` (or `raw`). Left out when no product carries it.

earliest.description: `date_out_of_range` only: the region's floor — nothing earlier is ever served. On `uk` 2026-10-15T00:00:00.000Z (the recorded data starts 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z: an instant between the two is 404 `no_history`); on an international code its archive's first day, 2026-11-16T00:00:00.000Z.

latest.description: `date_out_of_range` only: the archive's newest instant — its newest checkpoint's board version plus one hour (checkpoints are cut nightly for the previous UTC day).

error.description: `insufficient_tokens`: the request's price is above the account's balance. Nothing was served or spent. The message names the price, the balance and the reset, and two fixes: add filters, or (plans `pro` and `business`) talk to us about Enterprise at https://oddsrelay.io/contact, or (a custom plan) talk to us about raising your allowance at https://oddsrelay.io/contact, or (every other plan) upgrade. No `Retry-After`.

resets_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, whole seconds: when the pool resets; on a trial, the trial's end when that comes first.

quote.description: How to price a request for free.

upgrade_url.description: The account's billing page: where to upgrade, or on `pro` and `business` where to ask about Enterprise. Absent on a custom plan (any plan code but `free`, `trial`, `trial_outreach`, `starter`, `pro` and `business`): it has no self-serve upgrade.

remaining.description: Tokens left, `unlimited`, or null when unknown.

last_seen.description: `{bookmaker key: {sport key base: ISO-8601 Z}}`: the last instant each venue and sport was read, the oldest observation behind the board, so `now - last_seen` is an upper bound on that venue's price age. The region's venues only, cut to a filtered body's venues and sports; always ISO; absent until the board carries the table; never on `format=bare`.

MatchedEvent.description: One fixture. Ids are opaque and the same on every route: one fixture is one id, and that id never changes for it.

event_id.description: The event's id: opaque, one per fixture, the same on every route, and never changed once served, whatever its exchanges, spellings or kick-off do next. An id found to name the same fixture as one served earlier is merged into it and listed in that event's `previous_ids`.

sport_key.description: The sport, and the league its venues file the event under (`soccer_premier_league`; a horse race `horse_racing`). An event keeps the `sport_key` and `sport_title` it was first served with for as long as it is served (one that had no league may gain one once); filter a competition by `competition_key`. An event whose venues name no competition is served under its sport's catch-all key, the sport's name twice (`golf_golf`, `tennis_tennis`, `greyhound_racing_greyhound_racing`); horse racing is `horse_racing`.

competition_key.description: The event's COMPETITION: one key per competition, the same on every route that serves the event, built from what its venues call it (`sports=<this key>` returns the competition whole). Shaped `<sport>_<name>`, so a sport base still prefixes it. Null when no venue's name for it identifies one competition, and on every racing event. An event keeps the `competition_key` it was first served with for as long as it is served (a null may become a key once; a key never changes for the event), and a key is never renamed or reused.

previous_ids.description: The ids merged into this event: ids served for its fixture before they were found to be one fixture with it, on this board or on `/v2/odds/raw` (the same list raw serves). Often several for an event many bookmakers list; empty when none were; never this event's own id. Each answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds` as this event while this event is on the board, and again if its fixture is listed again within 60 days. Since 2026-11-14.

event_name.description: An event with no two teams that is not a horse race (a golf tournament, an outright): its name, and an ante-post race market: its category (`Ante-Post Cheltenham Festival`) — the same string every route serves for this id. A greyhound race keeps, on the matched boards that list one (`standard`), the name it was first served with — its UK off time and course (`21:04 Central Park`) — beside `venue`; `/v2/odds/raw`, the event route and `/v2/events` serve a greyhound race's `venue` alone, as for every race.

venue.description: Racing (horse and greyhound): the course, the same string every route serves for this id. One string per course (since 2026-11-14): its country tag in one spelling — `(AUS)`, `(US)`, `(NZL)`, `(HK)`, `(JPN)`… — an overseas course our course table holds tagged even when no bookmaker tags it (`Fukushima (JPN)`, `Woodbine (CAN)`; one it does not hold yet keeps the bookmakers' spelling), a UK or Irish course plain, and a greyhound track and a racecourse of one name two courses (`The Meadows (AUS)` greyhounds, `The Meadows (US)` harness); a greyhound meeting's words dropped (`Hove`, not `Hove Bags`). An ante-post market carries its festival's course (`Cheltenham`), or none, and its category as `event_name`.

in_play.description: `inPlay=only` only: `true` when the event's venues show it in play.

link.description: The venue's page for this event.

place_fraction.description: `each-way`, `extra-place`: the place terms as a fraction.

dutch_id.description: `dutching` only: 8 hex naming the dutch this leg belongs to. Group one market's offers by it and rate a dutch as 100 / sum(1/price).

lay.description: Lowest price first. An array of exchange offers; on `each-way` and `extra-place` an object `{win, place}` of two such arrays; absent on `dutching`.

available.description: Money available at that lay price.
Money available at that lay price.
Money available at that lay price.

RawOutcome.description: A bookmaker quote is `{name, price}`. An exchange's back quote is `{name, price, back_available}`; a venue quoting a lay side is `{name, back_price, lay_price, available}`, and racing's combined exchange row is `{name, back_price, lay_price, available, back_available}`. Both stakes are in GBP and are the BACKER'S STAKE that can be matched at that price at the venue's latest read, on every exchange (Betfair Exchange, Matchbook, Smarkets): `available` beside `lay_price` (a layer's liability there is `available` x (`lay_price` - 1)), `back_available` beside the back price (`price`, or racing's `back_price`). Both are left out under `includeLiquidity=false`, and `back_available` wherever the venue gave no back stake. No commission is applied. Where known, an outcome also carries `side` and `point` (both after every other field): `side` is which side of the EVENT the outcome is, `point` its line. Raw keeps every venue's own names, so on an h2h market `side` says which team a spelling names (`HOU Texans` under `Houston Texans v Indianapolis Colts` is `home`), and on a handicap market `side` is the truth while the word `Home` or `Away` in `name` is the BOOKMAKER's own listing order: venues list a US game either way round, so one venue's `Home +7.5 Points` can be the event's away team (`side: away`, `point: 7.5`).

side.description: Which side of the event this outcome is: `home` and `away` are the event's own `home_team` and `away_team` IN THIS SAME REPLY (read it against them, never against another region's reply: one event id can be listed the other way round on another region), `draw` the draw, `over` and `under` a total's. Given on h2h, 3-way h2h, draw-no-bet and half-time result markets (and their periods), handicaps and asian handicaps, and totals (`over_under` and its periods), each with its exchange `_lay` market; on a handicap it outranks the `Home`/`Away` in `name`. ABSENT means not applicable (other markets, races, outrights, an event with no teams) or NOT KNOWN: a side is given only when the venue's own listing places the outcome exactly, never guessed — absent never means "neither". It can appear later for an outcome that had none (the venue's listing is placed against the event once identified), and a value changes only when the venue really relists the match the other way round; never otherwise.

point.description: The line, exactly as `name` reads it: signed on a handicap (`Home -12.5 Points` is -12.5, `Away +7 Points` is 7), unsigned on a total (`Over 43.5 Points` is 43.5) — the same field as a matched outcome's `point`. On a handicap it is the line of the team `side` names, so the event's home team's even-money line has one sign at every venue whatever `name` says. Absent where the market has no line or `name` does not follow `<Home|Away|Over|Under> <line> [<unit>] [(<period>)]`; given even where `side` is not known.

id.description: The event's id: opaque, one per fixture, the same on every route, and never changed once served, whatever its exchanges, spellings or kick-off do next. An id found to name the same fixture as one served earlier is merged into it and listed in that event's `previous_ids`.

sport_key.description: The sport, and the league its venues file the event under (`soccer_premier_league`; a horse race `horse_racing`). An event keeps the `sport_key` and `sport_title` it was first served with for as long as it is served (one that had no league may gain one once); filter a competition by `competition_key`. An event whose venues name no competition is served under its sport's catch-all key, the sport's name twice (`golf_golf`, `tennis_tennis`, `greyhound_racing_greyhound_racing`); horse racing is `horse_racing`.

competition_key.description: The event's COMPETITION: one key per competition, the same on every route that serves the event, built from what its venues call it (`sports=<this key>` returns the competition whole). Shaped `<sport>_<name>`, so a sport base still prefixes it. Null when no venue's name for it identifies one competition, and on every racing event. An event keeps the `competition_key` it was first served with for as long as it is served (a null may become a key once; a key never changes for the event), and a key is never renamed or reused.

previous_ids.description: The ids merged into this event: ids served for its fixture before they were found to be one fixture with it. Often several for an event many bookmakers list; empty when none were; never this event's own id. Each answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds` as this event while this event is on the board, and again if its fixture is listed again within 60 days.

commence_time.description: The kick-off (UTC). It moves when the fixture is rescheduled: it follows the exchange where one lists the event, else most bookmakers.

home_team.description: Team sports: the side, kept under the id while any bookmaker still lists it that way (home and away never swap while one lists them in that order). Null on a race (see `venue`) and on an event with no two teams (see `event_name`).

tags.description: Historical odds, bookmakers and exchanges (`bookmakersOnly=true`: bookmakers alone): the board as of any instant since 2026-10-17 (nothing before 2026-10-15 is ever served), event histories, closing lines, bulk files. Released a UTC day at a time, the night after it (a later instant is 400 `date_out_of_range` with `latest`). Priced in tokens by /v2/pricing `regions.uk.historical` (an international region: its own `regions.<code>.historical` block). Each of the 20 international codes is its own archive of its own venues: bookmakers, and in `ca` also STX (`stx_ca`, Ontario's betting exchange, as /v2/odds/raw serves it there: its back prices under each market's key, its lay prices under `<key>_lay`; `bookmakersOnly=true` leaves it out, and a file's `bookmakers_only` says whether the file holds its rows), recorded from 2026-11-16T05:50Z, the lane's first checkpoint (its first day 2026-11-16: an instant before that day is 400 `date_out_of_range` with `earliest` 2026-11-16T00:00:00.000Z, one inside it before the first checkpoint 404 `no_history`), `gr` from its switch-on at 2026-11-16T18:19Z (a `gr` page asked for before it is empty, and free), with uk's tiers, release lag and rules. Exchanges (Betfair Exchange, Smarkets and Matchbook) are recorded from 2026-10-17 (the first whole day is 2026-10-18): each outcome's best back price, best lay price and `available` (the stake at the best lay) — no ladder, no traded volume; snapshots of an instant from 2026-11-06 17:53 UTC on also carry `back_available` (the stake at the best back), change rows do not. BETDAQ, which closed on 2026-10-21, is in no answer. The bulk files and the closing lines hold exchanges too (a file's `bookmakers_only` says whether it holds bookmakers alone). The event `id` is the only safe join between a bulk file, a history reply and the live routes: a file row's `sport_key` is the league recorded when the row was cut, a reply's the league the id is served with, and the two can differ.
